I make my own baby food for my 7-month-old, so I have become almost hyperaware of prices for fruits and vegetables. I live in a medium-sized city in Ontario, so I'm not in some little town in the middle of Bumfuck, Nowhere. All prices I'm listing are in Canadian Dollars.

Peas are probably one of the cheapest things I can make. I got a 950g bag of frozen peas for $2, which made about 24 ounces of baby food once I ground it all up. I worked it out to just over 8 cents an ounce. For reference, if I were to buy a jar of baby food at Walmart it would be about 20 cents an ounce. Carrots, sweet potato, and butternut squash are similarly priced. The other thing that's dirt cheap right now are apples, because they're in season. I bought an entire bushel of organic apples for $20 straight from the farm, and have been turning them into apple sauce for the little guy. There were at least 60 apples in that bushel.

Fruits tend to be more expensive than veggies. I bought a bag of frozen strawberries at Walmart for $5, and the yield was about 30oz. of baby food. I worked it out to 16 cents per ounce. That was probably one of the most expensive things I've made so far.
